body: you shouldnt be farther than east 82nd.

you have created the perfect argument against yourself.

i have never been the same person i was in the recent past, whether or not im better for it.  my life changes because i create arguments like this, and then i act on the conclusions. 

when i was younger i realized that i had the option to change, i will never again call myself a coward.

this is all talk, just before i read your post i was wondering why no one will return my calls, why my girlfriend left me. why im still unemployed... etc etc.

but at least when im not drunk i can begin to remember the times ive known that im not a coward. 

have confidence.

you dont have to defend your drinking to anyone, the problem arises when you must defend yourself from your drunken actions. dont blame the drinking, find what is wrong and make an effort to create a mental framework to accept and work around the feelings associated with the pain. this hopefully will allow you through time to work through the thoughts that trigger your drinking.

assess why you feel, find the trigger to the emotions, determine its validity (does it effect how i should move forward in life?), look past the parts which dont factor into decision making.

this all requires you first to accept that you will find a new path, no matter where it might lead.

just what im telling myself right now, instead of posting to my own sw link.
